clue.text: Tie up troops in creating chances of advancement

indicators.note: creating means making something new, so the letters of the preceding words are worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A general ties down his soldiers in order to open up openings for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' is the anagram signal; the thirteen letters of TIE UP TROOPS IN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Openings or favourable occasions for getting on in life are synonyms for this word.

clue.text: Job seeking

definitions.meaning: an occupation or activity one follows, as in a favourite leisure pastime
the act of chasing or searching after something, as in the hunt for happiness

explanation.surface: Looking for employment.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a hobby or occupation; the other is the act of chasing after a goal.

clue.text: Leader of Opposition, jerk, is of concern to the listener

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of Opposition is taken

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: The Leader of the Opposition, a jerk, is something the audience should worry about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Opposition' looks like a political title but just gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means relating to the ear, the organ a listener uses.

clue.text: Tool he'd fashioned, something of use to climbers

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters of the words before it are reshaped

explanation.surface: A craftsman has made a tool that climbers will find handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges TOOLHED, the letters of 'Tool he'd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ledge or crevice giving purchase for a foot is what a mountaineer seeks on a rock face.

clue.text: Tangled in hedge, sounded like a farm animal

indicators.note: tangled means twisted up and jumbled, so the letters of the words that follow are mixed

explanation.surface: A horse caught up in a hedge gave a cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: INHEDGE is rearranged under 'Tangled'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the cry a horse makes, and horses are kept on farms.

clue.text: You can catch trout in it, or try

definitions.text: You can catch trout in it
definitions.meaning: the river of this name in Hampshire, southern England, is a famous trout-fishing chalk stream
to try something out is to put it to a trial

explanation.surface: An angler's tip: the river's full of trout, so have a go.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a river in Hampshire, England, renowned for fly fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense names an English trout river; the other is a verb for trial or examination.

clue.text: Gave Len unusually good news!

indicators.note: unusually means in an uncommon way, so the letters of the two words before it are put in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly gave Len some welcome tidings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges GAVELEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek for glad tidings, the gospel message.

clue.text: The full version of Mass

parts.note: Mass looks like the church service, but with its capital it is the standard abbreviation of a US state, written out in full here

explanation.surface: Seems to ask for the complete liturgy of the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as the religious service; it is the postal-style abbreviation of the New England state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass. is the conventional shortening of this US state's name.

clue.text: Pun, or a charade perhaps

definitions.meaning: a joke exploiting double meanings of language
the parlour game of charades acts out syllables, a kind of verbal game; also a type of crossword clue built from word pieces

explanation.surface: A quibble, or a party game, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a quip on double meanings and a syllable-acting game are examples of toying with language.

clue.text: Transport system that's essential to divers

definitions.meaning: a company operating scheduled flights
read as two words, the hose that feeds breathing gas to a diver underwater

explanation.surface: A network that underwater swimmers cannot do without.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as AIR LINE, the tube supplying a diver with breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrier of passengers by aeroplane is one meaning; a breathing hose for divers is the other.

clue.text: This month, everyone is to get ready to work

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old business-letter shorthand for the current month
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A notice: this month everybody must prepare to start their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inst.' (instant) was formal letter-writing shorthand for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up equipment so it is operational is to fit it in place ready for use.

clue.text: A slow mover that may be fired

definitions.meaning: a garden mollusc famous for its sluggish crawl
a bullet, which is shot from a gun

explanation.surface: A sluggish employee who could get the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests dismissal from a job; here it means shot from a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a shell-less snail-like creature; the other is a bullet.

clue.text: They don't do themselves any good when they come to light

definitions.text: They don't do themselves any good when they come to light

parts.words: They don't do themselves any good when they come to light
parts.note: sounds like wrongdoers exposed, but describes night insects drawn fatally to lamps and flames

explanation.surface: Secrets that harm their keepers once revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to light' suggests being discovered; literally these insects fly to a lamp and get burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: These nocturnal insects are notoriously attracted to flames, often to their cost.

clue.text: To describe someone thus is hardly fair comment

definitions.text: To describe someone thus is hardly fair comment

parts.words: To describe someone thus is hardly fair comment
parts.note: fair comment is a legal phrase for justified criticism, but fair here also means good-looking, so the description is its opposite

explanation.surface: A remark about someone that seems unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' plays on just versus beautiful; calling someone unattractive is the opposite of calling them fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Unattractive in appearance is the opposite of fair in the old sense of beautiful.

clue.text: They're taken for trips?

parts.note: trips sounds like journeys, but is slang for hallucinogenic experiences

explanation.surface: Things like luggage or tickets taken on journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trips' in slang means hallucinatory experiences from narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics such as LSD are swallowed to induce a hallucinogenic experience.

clue.text: Ian follows a number of birds

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the name Ian is placed after the other pieces

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
the given name, taken as written

explanation.surface: Ian trails behind a group of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number of birds' looks like a flock, but 'a number' gives A and V (five).
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means relating to the class of feathered creatures.

clue.text: Made provisional arrangements

parts.note: provisional suggests temporary, but here relates to provisions, that is food supplied

explanation.surface: Set up some temporary plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provisional' normally means tentative; read as 'of provisions', it means supplying food.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply food and drink for an event is to arrange the provisions.

clue.text: Work in the dark to get negative results

definitions.text: Work in the dark to get negative results

parts.words: Work in the dark to get negative results
parts.note: sounds like fruitless effort, but describes processing film in a darkroom to produce negatives

explanation.surface: Labouring blindly only to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negative results' sounds like failure; in photography, film is processed in a darkroom to give negatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating exposed film with chemicals to bring out the image is the photographer's term.

clue.text: Moral support

definitions.meaning: honest and principled, as in a decent citizen
a vertical post or strut holding up a structure

explanation.surface: Encouragement given to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral support' reads as one phrase but splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is honourable and virtuous; the other is a vertical prop or post.

clue.text: Rebuff salesman going to one university after another

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
U is the abbreviation for university
another university: the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A salesman doing the rounds of the campuses is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE is the London School of Economics, part of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back or reject is a synonym for rebuff.

clue.text: Pontoon player who cheats?

definitions.meaning: in pontoon, a card game like blackjack, a player who says twist takes another card
a swindler or crook

explanation.surface: A card player who isn't playing straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for blackjack; asking to 'twist' means taking another card.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a card player taking another card; the other is a dishonest trickster.

clue.text: Leave with music playing

parts.note: having a band, a group of musicians, in attendance
on means performing, as an act is on stage

explanation.surface: Depart while the band strikes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay splits as A BAND ON: with musicians performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert or forsake is to go away from and never return.

clue.text: Assign work to a writer

parts.note: a scribe is one who writes or copies documents

explanation.surface: Attribute a piece of work to an author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work to' only joins the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute or credit something to a cause or person is to assign it.

clue.text: Justify rate

definitions.meaning: to warrant or earn, as conduct may warrant praise
to merit, as a story rates a mention

explanation.surface: Account for a price level.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to be worthy of or merit something.

clue.text: Eastern agent gets notice

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy

explanation.surface: An operative from the East receives a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a noun (a written warning) but is the verb, to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of is to spot or observe.

clue.text: Charming woman but bad speller

definitions.meaning: charming in the literal sense: one who casts charms, a sorceress
one who casts evil spells

explanation.surface: A delightful lady who can't spell properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speller' suggests orthography; it means a caster of spells, and a malign one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorceress both works charms and casts wicked enchantments.

clue.text: Capital required, so backed with a pound, nothing more

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the word so is turned around

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Money is needed, so a financial backer supplies a pound and no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'pound' suggest money; Capital is the city. 'more' just tacks O on.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Norway.

clue.text: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter

definitions.text: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter

parts.words: Quarrel that can be relatively bitter
parts.note: relatively seems to mean comparatively, but hints at relatives, as in a long-running family vendetta

explanation.surface: A dispute that may be fairly acrimonious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' suggests 'fairly'; it hints at relatives, since such vendettas often run in families.
explanation.definitionFit: A prolonged bitter enmity, often between families or clans, is this kind of quarrel.

clue.text: Mumble an insult?

definitions.meaning: to speak indistinctly, running words together
a slight or disparaging remark

explanation.surface: Muttering something rude.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to speak indistinctly; the other is a derogatory remark.

clue.text: A couple of students entertained by exam topping the rest

indicators.note: entertained by means hosted inside, so the earlier pieces go within the exam word

parts.note: a test is an exam
L is the learner, a student; a couple gives two

explanation.surface: Two students are hosted by an exam board and outperform everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner (the L-plate on a learner driver's car) counts as a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatest in height means rising above everyone else.

clue.text: Denied a civil education

parts.note: civil reads as civic or civil service, but means polite: a person never taught manners

explanation.surface: Refused schooling in civics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'civil' suggests citizenship; it means courteous, so the person was raised without manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and lacking in manners because of a poor upbringing.

clue.text: Soft-centred?

parts.note: sounds like a chocolate, but the centre is the heart, and soft means kind

explanation.surface: A description of a chocolate with a gooey filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft-centred' describes a confection; read as a person, their core (heart) is gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kind and easily moved to compassion, with a gentle core.
